{{nihongo|'''Hida-Ichinomiya Minashi Shrine''' |飛騨一宮水無神社|Hida Ichinomiya Minashi Jinja}}, commonly: {{nihongo|'''Minashi Shrine'''|水無神社|Minashi Jinja}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in the Ichinomiya neighborhood of the city of {{ill|Takayama, Gifu|en|Takayama, Gifu|qid=Q622594|lt=Takayama|1=Takayama, Gifu}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|en|Gifu Prefecture|qid=Q131277|lt=Gifu Prefecture|1=Gifu Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}.  It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the former {{ill|Hida Province|en|Hida Province|qid=Q1056535|lt=Hida Province|1=Hida Province}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on May 2.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}}</ref> 
==Enshrined ''kami''==
The primary ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Minashi Jinja is:
* {{nihongo|'''[[Toshigami]]'''| 御歳大神 |}}, the god of the year.
==History==
There are no official records marking the construction of the shrine; however, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|en|Emperor Seiwa|qid=Q349243|lt=Emperor Seiwa|1=Emperor Seiwa}} (858–878), the shrine appears in official records and was given Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade [[List of Japanese court Ranks, positions and hereditary titles|court Rank]]. The shrine is listed in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' records. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}}, it was referred toes the "Minashi Dai-gongen" and in the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period|1=Muromachi period}} as the "Minashi Myōjin" or the "Minashi Hachiman". During the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|qid=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto|1=State Shinto}}, the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank |国幣小社|Kokuhei Shosha}} under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]] from 1871. From 1874 to 1877, {{ill|Shimazaki Masaki|en|Shimazaki Masaki|qid=Q105711327|lt=Shimazaki Masaki|1=Shimazaki Masaki}}, the father of author {{ill|Tōson Shimazaki|en|Tōson Shimazaki|qid=Q1093783|lt=Shimazaki Tōson|1=Tōson Shimazaki}} and model for the main character of his seminal work {{ill|Before the Dawn (novel)|en|Before the Dawn (novel)|qid=Q4880345|lt=''Before the Dawn''|1=Before the Dawn (novel)}} was the ''[[kannushi]]'' of this shrine.<ref name="Yoshiki">{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}}</ref>
Because of the [[:en:Bombing of Nagoya in World War II|Bombing of Nagoya in World War II]], Minashi Shrine served as a refuge for [[:en:Atsuta Jingu|Atsuta Jingu]]'s ''[[Kusanagi no Tsurugi|Kusanagi]]'' from August 21 to September 19, 1945.
The shrine is located an eight-minute walk from {{ill|Hida-Ichinomiya Station|en|Hida-Ichinomiya Station|qid=Q5751478|lt=Hida-Ichinomiya Station|1=Hida-Ichinomiya Station}} on the [[:en:JR Central|JR Central]] {{ill|Takayama Main Line|en|Takayama Main Line|qid=Q1188357|lt=Takayama Main Line|1=Takayama Main Line}}.<ref name="Okada">{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}}</ref>
